issues.failure_explanation: For fixed $n_2$ and $F$, $\Gamma_{n_2,n_1}(F)=\{z\in\mathcal{G}_{n_2}:h_{n_2,n_1}(z,F)<\varepsilon-1/n_2\}$ is a subset of a finite grid, and only pointwise convergence $h_{n_2,n_1}(z,F)\to h_{n_2}(z,F)$ is established. A grid point $z$ with $h_{n_2}(z,F)$ exactly equal to $\varepsilon-1/n_2$ can have $h_{n_2,n_1}(z,F)$ oscillating on both sides of the strict threshold, so the sequence of subsets need not converge at all; and when it does converge, the limit is $\{h_{n_2}\le\varepsilon-1/n_2\}$ up to boundary points, not the claimed $\{h_{n_2}<\varepsilon-1/n_2\}$. Hence the asserted pointwise set-limit may not exist, its identification is wrong at the boundary, and the sandwich in Step 3(d) ($\{r_F\le\varepsilon-2/n_2\}\subset\Gamma_{n_2}(F)$) has the same strictness defect. The tower as defined may therefore fail to be a valid tower.

failure_location.quote:
Consequently, for each fixed $n_2$ the pointwise set-limit exists:
\[
\Gamma_{n_2}(F):=\lim_{n_1\to\infty}\Gamma_{n_2,n_1}(F)
=\Bigl\{z\in\mathcal{G}_{n_2}:\ h_{n_2}(z,F)<\varepsilon-\frac1{n_2}\Bigr\}.
\]

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Adjust the inner threshold to $\varepsilon-1/n_2+1/n_1$ (equivalently use non-strict tests with slack); then on the finite grid the inner limit exists and equals $\{h_{n_2}\le\varepsilon-1/n_2\}$, the Step 3(d) inclusions hold at the boundary, and the Hausdorff-convergence conclusion is unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The height-2/height-1 tower construction for $\Xi_{\sigma_{\mathrm{ap}},\varepsilon}$ in the meta theorem is unjustified as written; the claimed $\mathrm{SCI}_G$ upper bounds (2 on $\Omega_{\mathcal X},\Omega_{\mathcal X}^m$, 1 on the modulus classes) are unaffected once the threshold slack is fixed.
issues.title: Meta-theorem: inner tower limit may fail to exist (strict threshold on a finite grid)
issues.why_classification: A one-line threshold adjustment makes the inner limit exist on the finite grid and restores the sandwich; the SCI bounds, method, and advertised scope all survive, so the repair is short, local, and routine.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Because $W$ is finite-dimensional, all norms on $W$ are equivalent. In particular,
$S$ is compact in $(W,\|\cdot\|_\infty)$, and the inclusion $W\hookrightarrow C(\X)$ is
continuous.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof asserts that $S=\{h\in W:\|h\|_{L^1(\omega)}=1\}$ is compact in the sup-norm 'because all norms on the finite-dimensional $W$ are equivalent'. This requires $\|\cdot\|_{L^1(\omega)}$ to be a genuine norm on $W$ (equivalently on $C(\mathcal X)$), i.e. full support of $\omega$. Without it, $\|\cdot\|_{L^1}$ is only a seminorm and $S$ can be unbounded in the sup-norm: e.g. $\mathcal X=[0,1]$, $\omega=\delta_0$, $W=\mathrm{span}\{1,x\}$ gives $S=\{a+bx:|a|=1\}$, and for any deterministic quadrature with $x_{P_0}\neq 0$ on the cell containing $0$, $Q_n(|1+bx|)=|1+b\,x_{P_0}|$, so $\sup_{h\in S}|Q_n(|h|)-\|h\|_1|=\infty$ for every $n$. The uniform convergence is false under the stated hypotheses (compact metric space, finite Borel measure); the conclusion holds once $\operatorname{supp}\omega=\mathcal X$ is assumed.

failure_location.quote:
Then for every finite-dimensional subspace $W\subset C(\X)$ one has
\[
   \sup_{\substack{h\in W\\ \|h\|_{L^1(\omega)}=1}}
   \Bigl|\,Q_n(|h|)\\;-\;\|h\|_{L^1(\omega)}\,\Bigr|
   \xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{} 0 .
\]

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that $\omega$ has full support ($\operatorname{supp}\omega=\mathcal X$), equivalently that $\|\cdot\|_{L^1(\omega)}$ is a norm on $C(\mathcal X)$; then $S$ is compact in the sup-norm, the Arzel\`a--Ascoli equicontinuity step is valid, and the conclusion follows as written.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed sufficient condition for axiom (F2) in the $L^1$ endpoint is not valid under the stated hypotheses, and the accompanying remark that '(F2) can be satisfied' in $L^1$ is too broad. All applications with full-support measures (e.g. the Bernoulli measure on $2^{\mathbb N}$ used throughout the paper) are unaffected, and the meta theorem is conditional on (F1)-(F4) in any case.
issues.title: L^1 quadrature lemma lacks a full-support hypothesis and is false as stated
issues.why_classification: Adding the standard full-support condition is a short, local repair that validates the existing proof; every application in the paper uses full-support measures, so no substantive claim, rate, or advertised scope is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Consequently, the set
\[
B_{n_k,\ldots,n_1}:=\{F:\Gamma_{n_k,\ldots,n_1}(F)=1\}
\]
is a finite Boolean combination of cylinder sets of the form
$\{F: (f_{j_1}(F),\ldots,f_{j_m}(F))\in U\}$ with $U\subset\C^m$ Borel; hence $B_{n_k,\ldots,n_1}$
is Borel in $\Omega_\X^\infty$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof's base case concludes that each base-algorithm acceptance set is Borel only because it is a finite Boolean combination of cylinders $\{F:(f_{j_1}(F),\dots,f_{j_m}(F))\in U\}$; such cylinders are Borel only if the evaluations $f_j$ are Borel measurable, which is not assumed for an arbitrary countable $\Lambda$ and can fail. Moreover the statement is false as written: taking $\Lambda=\{\mathbf 1_{A_{z_0}}\}$ (a single evaluation equal to the characteristic function of the acceptance set) lets a base algorithm query that one evaluation and output the answer, giving $\mathrm{SCI}_A=0$, not $\infty$. The theorem is valid only after restricting $\Lambda$ to Borel (e.g. continuous, or the point-evaluation/quadrature) evaluations.

failure_location.quote:
where $\{0,1\}$ is equipped with the discrete metric and $\Lambda$ is a \textit{countable} evaluation
set.
Then the solvability complexity index of the decision problem is infinite in the arithmetic model, i.e.
\[
\mathrm{SCI}\bigl(\Xi_{z_0},\Omega_\X^\infty,\{0,1\},\Lambda\bigr)_{A}=\infty.
\]

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the evaluation set to Borel (e.g. continuous) evaluations -- in particular the point-evaluation/quadrature oracle $\Lambda_{\rm pt}\cup\Lambda_{\rm quad}$ used elsewhere in the paper; then the base-case Borelness argument is valid and the proof yields $\mathrm{SCI}_A=\infty$. Without such a hypothesis the statement is false.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised scope 'any countable oracle model' (also claimed in the introduction) is false; the lower bound $\mathrm{SCI}_A=\infty$ survives only for Borel/continuous evaluations such as the intended point-evaluation plus quadrature oracle. The theorem's conclusion is additionally invalidated by the false Silver equivalence (ISSUE-005), which is listed there.
issues.title: Type-A decision lower bound is false for arbitrary countable evaluation sets
issues.why_classification: The repair adds a necessary hypothesis to the theorem (Borel evaluations) and withdraws the advertised 'any countable oracle model' scope, but the intended lower bound for the point-evaluation oracle survives intact; the burden is a contained hypothesis addition, not a new proof architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Fix a base-level algorithm in the tower. By definition, it queries finitely many
point evaluations $F\mapsto F(x_1),\dots,F(x_N)$ and then applies an arbitrary
postprocessing map.

issues.failure_explanation: In the type-G model a base algorithm may choose its finite query set depending on the input, with arbitrary post-processing. The proof only uses that each fixed evaluation $F_S(x)$ depends on $S\cap 2^{M(x)}$, but the queried points $x_j=x_j(F_S)$ themselves vary with $S$ through the arbitrary query-selection map, so $S\mapsto\Gamma(F_S)$ need not be locally constant or Borel; hence the restricted tower is not a Borel tower and thm:borel_tower_implies_borel_target cannot be applied. This is exactly the phenomenon the paper's own 'Logical Insight' section warns about: descriptive-set hardness does not by itself yield type-G lower bounds. A genuine Baire-category uniformisation argument is needed to rescue the proof.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Supply the iterated Baire-category uniformisation argument (the technique the introduction advertises, in the spirit of ben2015computing Section 10) showing that any type-G tower computing $\sigma_{\mathrm{ap}}$ on the coded family $\{F_S\}$ yields a Borel selection, contradicting the non-Borelness of the acceptance set; the simple restriction-to-Borel-tower step cannot be justified and must be replaced.
issues.overall_effect: The central type-G lower bound $\mathrm{SCI}_G=\infty$ for $L^\infty$ Koopman $\sigma_{\mathrm{ap}}$ on $\Omega_\X^m$ (and hence on $\Omega_\X$) is unproven as written; the corollary for the $\alpha$-classes inherits the same gap via its 'applies verbatim' reduction. The conclusion may survive, but only via a new argument; this defect is independent of the false Silver equivalence (ISSUE-005), which also invalidates the same theorem.
issues.title: Type-G lower bound: the restricted tower need not be Borel (adaptive query selection)
issues.why_classification: The conclusion and advertised regime may survive, but the proof requires a contained yet nontrivial new argument (Baire-category uniformisation) to replace the unjustified Borel-restriction step; no global change of statement and no major loss, but the current proof cannot be patched locally.

$u_{m-1}(S)\frown \ast,\ u_{m-1}(S)\frown 0,\ u_{m-1}(S)\frown 1$,

But $u_1(S)=*$, $u_2(S)=*0$, and all three level-3 extensions fail because $10$ is a dead end: $\Sigma(*0*)

failure_location.quote:
By the star-priority construction of $u_m(S)$ (it chooses $\ast$ whenever that choice preserves
$\Sigma(\cdot)\\subseteq S\cap 2^m$), the pattern $u_m(S)$ has at least as many $\ast$-coordinates as
any admissible witness pattern.
In particular,
\[
k_m(S)=|u_m(S)|_\ast \ \ge\ |w_m|_\ast\ =\ |m\setminus A|.
\]

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair: the defect is in the construction itself, since the dynamics $F_S$ cannot detect Silver-tree containment when $S$ has dead-end branches. A repair requires a new tree-to-dynamics construction together with a new descriptive-set front end for the corrected target set; the false equivalence cannot be patched locally.
issues.overall_effect: The central reduction $S\in\mathcal V\iff z_0\in\sigma_{\mathrm{ap}}(\K_{F_S})$ is false in the forward direction, so the entire $L^\infty$ lower-bound program collapses: the Cantor transfer, the Silver reduction, the analytic-completeness route (thm:route-IF-to-Az0), the type-A decision lower bound (thm:SCI_A_infty_Linfty_decision), the type-G lower bounds on the $m$-classes and $\alpha$-classes, and the corresponding abstract/introduction claims all become unreliable. The Borel-tower gap (ISSUE-004) is independent and would remain even if the equivalence were repaired.
issues.title: Forward Silver-tree reduction is false: dead ends destroy the star-priority witness
issues.why_classification: The primary claim is false with a concrete counterexample, the defect is in the construction rather than a proof detail, and every $L^\infty$ lower bound in the paper (type-A and type-G) plus the analytic-completeness route is abandoned; no comparable version of the primary claim survives without a new construction and a new reduction source.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Let $\Omega_1$ carry the product topology generated by cylinder sets $E(\sigma)$.
Let $\Xi:\Omega_1\to\{0,1\}$ be computed by a height-$k$ tower of general algorithms, i.e.\ $\Xi\in\Delta_k^G$.

issues.failure_explanation: The base case asserts that a type-G general algorithm on $\Omega_1$ is locally constant on cylinders, so its acceptance set is clopen ($\Delta^0_1$). This is false under the cited framework (colbrook2024limits, Def. A.3): the query set may depend on the input and the post-processing is arbitrary. Counterexample on $\{0,1\}^{\mathbb N}$ with coordinate evaluations: $\Gamma(A)=1$ iff $A=1^\infty$ or the first zero of $A$ occurs at an even position, with query set $E(A)=\{0\}$ if $A=1^\infty$ and $E(A)=\{0,\dots,k(A)\}$ otherwise ($k(A)$ = first-zero position). Any two inputs agreeing on the union of their query sets have equal outputs, so $\Gamma$ is a general algorithm; but $\Gamma^{-1}(1)=\{1^\infty\}\cup\{k(A)\\text{ even}\}$ is $\Pi^0_1\setminus\Sigma^0_1$, not clopen. Hence the induction starts from a false base, and the lower bound $\Xi_m\notin\Delta_{m-1}^G$ is unproven.

failure_location.quote:
\textbf{Base $k=0$:}
If $\Xi$ is a general algorithm, then by local constancy on cylinders,
$\Xi^{-1}(1)$ is a union of cylinder sets, hence open.
Applying the same to $1-\Xi$ shows $\Xi^{-1}(0)$ is open, so $\Xi^{-1}(1)$ is also closed.
Hence $\Xi^{-1}(1)$ is clopen, i.e.\ $\Delta^0_1$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the base case by a correct complexity analysis of type-G general algorithms on the Cantor cube (acceptance sets need not be clopen, as the first-zero-parity example shows) and re-prove the lower bound; the source provides no such analysis, and its own Logical-Insight section warns that descriptive-set arguments do not by themselves yield type-G lower bounds, so the exact-height claim may only be recoverable in weakened form.
issues.overall_effect: The implication 'tower height $k$ implies acceptance set in $\Delta^0_{k+1}$' is unproven, so the lower bound $\Xi_m\notin\Delta_{m-1}^G$ -- equivalently $\mathrm{SCI}_G(\Xi_m)=m$, the advertised 'exact finite tower height' of the family -- is unsupported; the introduction's claim of exact finite type-G heights is a consequence. The upper bound $\mathrm{SCI}_G(\Xi_m)\\le m$ (prop:Xi-upper-bound) and the $\Sigma^0_m$-completeness (lem:Xi_m_Sigma_complete) survive.
issues.title: Borel ambiguity lemma: base case false (type-G algorithms need not be locally constant)
issues.why_classification: The false step is confined to the base case; the family still provides height-$m$ towers and the predicates remain $\Sigma^0_m$-complete, so a corrected base-complexity analysis or a new lower-bound argument leaves a recognizably comparable result (arbitrarily large finite SCI heights), at most with a one-level loss in the exact height claim; the upper-bound half is unaffected.
